Learn more Black Friday is still a few days away, but as in recent years, the deals are going live earlier and earlier. That’s especially true in the audio world, as many of the biggest names are already having massive sales on their best and most popular speakers. Welcome to Shop Smarter : A series dedicated to highlighting not just what’s on sale, but why it’s worth owning. Discover more here . Sonos , for example, is having a massive sale on pretty much every speaker, soundbar, and subwoofer that it sells. The deals run through November 30th. Klipsch is another one. The American audio brand is currently discounting its various loudspeaker lineups, as well as its desktop speakers, portable Bluetooth speakers and soundbars. But that’s just the tip of the iceberg. Below, we’ve highlighted some of the most important Black Friday speaker deals that are live right now. Sonos Save $60 Sonos Play The Sonos Play is a portable speaker that’s sized (and priced) between the company’s Roam 2 and Move 2, and it works quite similarly to both. It has Bluetooth and Wi-Fi streaming capabilities, so you can integrate it with your home’s existing Sonos system or use it as a standalone Bluetooth speaker outside. Like the Move 2, the USB-C port on the Play’s back supports charging and line-in audio, so you can connect it directly to your computer or turntable (with a built-in preamplifier) and use it as a wired speaker. read more $239 at Sonos $299 (20% off) Audioengine Save $66 Audioengine A2+ Gen 3 The Audioengine A2+ Gen 3 is an upgraded version of the A2+ Next Gen. It’s the same compact speaker system, with each speaker pairing a 0.75-inch silk-dome tweeter with a 2.75-inch aramid-fiber woofer. However, the new models add support for an upgraded Bluetooth codec (aptX Adaptive) that Audioengine claims “dynamically adjusts transmission based on the audio content and wireless environment.” Additionally, Audioengine has switched from Class AB to Class D amplification, which the brand calls “the most significant amplifier” update to the A2+ series. read more $233 at Audioengine $299 (22% off) Bose Save $50 Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker is the company’s new entry-level smart speaker with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth streaming capabilities. It also has an auxiliary jack, so you can use it as a wired speaker with a computer or turntable. As a standalone mono speaker, it features two front-firing and one up-firing driver. For the best stereo experience, you can configure two in a stereo pair. In Sonos terms, it can best be described as a hybrid between the Era 100 ($219) and Era 300 ($449) smart speakers. read more $299 at Bose $349 (14% off) Amazon Save $800 KEF LS50 Wireless II Released in late 2020, the LS50 Wireless II is essentially an updated and better-sounding version of the LS50 Wireless (released in 2018). They use the company’s new proprietary Metamaterial Absorption Technology (MAT), which significantly reduces distortion. They have a new cone neck decoupler and motor system, which, again, helps eliminate distortion. The cabinet size has also been adjusted to give the speakers more bass. Thanks to an integrated HDMI eARC connection, they can easily be connected to a TV to add impressive sound to movies and games. read more $2,199 at Amazon $2,999 (27% off) $2,199 at KEF $2,999 (27% off) Sonos Save $160 Sonos Five Released in 2020, the Five is the largest and most hi-fi standalone speaker (that’s not a soundbar) that Sonos makes. It’s also pretty unique because it has a 3.5mm line-in connection so you can quickly connect it to an integrated turntable. And you can still pair two Fives together and place them vertically, which then designates them as right and left channels for great stereo sound. read more $439 at Sonos $599 (27% off) $439 at Amazon $599 (27% off) Klipsch Save $500 Klipsch The Fives II The Fives II are the smallest siblings to Klipsch’s The Sevens II and The Nines II. Like those, the Fives II is a wireless active speaker system with a vintage, mid-century aesthetic inspired by Klipsch’s iconic Heritage loudspeaker range. They support Wi-Fi streaming (as well as Bluetooth), allowing you to stream higher-resolution audio (up to 24-bit/96kHz) via AirPlay 2, Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, Qobuz Connect, and Google Cast. read more $900 at Klipsch $1,400 (36% off) Sonos Save $250 Sonos Arc Ultra The Sonos Arc Ultra is the company’s flagship Dolby Atmos soundbar. It looks quite similar to the older Arc, but packs more drivers, has a redesigned center channel, and takes advanced of a new woofer technology called “Sound Motion.” This helps the Arc Ultra deliver better midrange and more bass than the Arc, despite being similar in size. read more $849 at Sonos $1,099 (23% off) $849 at Amazon $1,099 (23% off) KEF Save $300 KEF Q1 Meta In 2024, KEF overhauled its most entry-level loudspeaker with the same driver and technology used in its higher-end R Series Meta range. The result is an impressive hi-fi upgrade that punches well above its weight class, that maintains the minimalist design the brand is known for. In other words, this is a perfect choice for audiophiles or home theater enthusiasts seeking accuracy and contemporary style in a compact package. And though this set used to retail for $600 before tariffs, it’s still a nice deal at $400. read more $400 at Amazon $700 (43% off) $400 at KEF $700 (43% off) JBL Save $50 JBL Flip 7 The JBL Flip 7 is a new-and-improved version of its 2021-released predecessor, the Flip 6. The portable Bluetooth speaker features a similar design but several under-the-hood upgrades. It has an IP68 rating and promises up to 14 hours on a single charge, a slight upgrade over the Flip 6’s IP67 rating and 12-hour battery life. It also has an upgraded tweeter and supports JBL’s AI Sound Boost, a technology that JBL has featured in its higher-end speakers that leverages AI to maximize sound quality while limiting distortion. read more $100 at JBL $150 (33% off) Klipsch Save $850 Klipsch The Nines II Klipsch’s The Nines II is a second-generation version of the brand’s 2023-released The Nines. Like before, it’s a large powered speaker system with a vintage-inspired design, but it’s upgraded with Onkyo’s electronics and amplification, Wi-Fi streaming capabilities, and support for Dolby Atmos and thus promises to be a better TV speaker system. title: Noble Audio Just Gave Audiophiles a Fresh Reason to Get Serious About Wired Hi-Fi
summary: The Texas-based audio specialist's newest hi-fi headphones are inspired by a medieval knight's armor.
content: The Texas-based audio specialist’s newest hi-fi headphones are inspired by a medieval knight’s armor. Noble Audio If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Noble Audio is on a heater. Earlier this month, the Texas-based hi-fi specialist introduced the Astrid , a new pair of beautifully designed wireless earbuds with a three-driver hybrid design. Positioned as an AirPods Pro alternative for audiophiles, they cost $539. Now, Noble Audio is getting back to its in-ear monitor (IEM) roots with a new high-end pair, the Paladin , that is equal parts striking and expensive. They’re designed for serious audiophiles looking for a lavish pair of in-ear monitors. The Paladin combines eight balanced armatures, two Sonion bone-conduction drivers and two Super-Magnetic planar drivers in each earpiece. Noble Audio Is that chainmail? There’s only one place to start: the design. The Paladin is a high-end pair of in-ear monitors that are wrapped in shining armor, literally. The IEMs get their name from a paladin, a medieval knight, and thus Noble Audio has given them a distinctive appearance meant to look like chainmail. It consists of a woven pattern of small, interlocking rings with silver-finished resin shells. This armored finish extends to the rest of the Paladin. Each earpiece has an integrated stainless steel wax guard that protects the nozzle. And the supplied 1.3-meter custom Litz Type 4S cable has 3D shielding. The detachable cable terminates in a 4.4 mm balanced plug. Noble Audio The Paladin features silver-finished resin shells with a chainmail-inspired weave and a custom cable to match. Noble Audio Noble claims that the 12-driver array helps the Paladin keep voices and instruments natural and reveal the finer details in a recording. Noble Audio 12-driver array Naturally, the Paladin is certified audiophile-grade. Each earbud has a 12-driver tribrid configuration comprising eight balanced armatures, two Sonion bone-conduction drivers and two Super-Magnetic planar drivers. A multi-way passive crossover brings the three driver technologies together. According to the brand, its aim with the Paladin was to “give bass its full weight, keep voices and instruments in proportion and let fine details come through at the top end.” Noble specifies that the Paladin has a frequency response of 12 Hz to 45 kHz. Impedance is rated at 21 ohms and sensitivity at 117 dB SPL/mW (both measured at 1 kHz). The supplied cable attaches to the Paladin’s earpieces via standard 0.78 mm two-pin connectors and terminates in a 4.4 mm balanced plug. This makes the Paladin work with a wide array of compatible audio players, DACs and headphone amplifiers. Noble says the Paladin’s conductors combine 5N OCC silver, palladium-plated 4N pure silver, a gold-silver-copper-palladium alloy, silver-plated 7N OCC copper and silver-plated 5N LCOFC copper. Noble Audio The Noble emblem sits on each faceplate against the fine silver pattern. Noble Audio Price and availability Noble Audio’s Paladin IEMs cost $3,500, making them one of the company’s more expensive IEMs. They are available for preorder now and will start shipping in early December. title: Yamaha’s Affordable Stereo Receiver Is Designed for Traditional Hi-Fi Beginners
summary: The Japanese hi-fi giant has revamped its budget-friendly stereo receiver for the first time in over a decade.
content: The Japanese hi-fi giant has revamped its budget-friendly stereo receiver for the first time in over a decade. Yamaha If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more In early October, Yamaha revealed an updated version of its most entry-level stereo receiver. The all-new R200A replaces the R-S202 , which was released in 2016. Like its predecessor, it’s designed for those who want to build a traditional stereo hi-fi system on a budget. Fast forward nearly two months, and the R200A stereo receiver is finally available for purchase. After more than a decade, Yamaha has upgraded its most entry-level stereo receiver. Yamaha Meet Yamaha’s new entry-level stereo receiver The Yamaha R200A is a two-channel stereo receiver that’s capable of outputting 100 watts (into 8 ohms per channel), allowing it to drive a wide variety of bookshelf and floorstanding loudspeakers. Since the previous model was released over a decade ago, the Japanese hi-fi maker has made wholesale acoustic improvements to the R200A. It features enhanced grounding circuitry, a newly designed heat sink and upgraded binding-post speaker terminals. Yamaha redesigned its entry-level stereo receiver both inside and out. Yamaha But arguably the biggest difference is with the connections. The R200A adds a direct phono input and a dedicated subwoofer output, making it easier to connect a turntable or add bass to the system. Additionally, the R200A also adds a flexible A/B speaker selection, so you can connect two pairs of passive speakers at the same time and switch between them. The R200A supports a wide range of analog and digital connections for both classic and modern audio sources. Yamaha Yamaha also upgraded the R200A with Bluetooth Multipoint, so you can wirelessly connect your smartphone and computer to the receiver and seamlessly switch between the two sources. Aesthetically, the R200A looks very different from the R-S202. Yamaha completely redesigned the front panel, with fewer (but larger) buttons and the small display moved to the bottom edge. The R200A features a new phono input and subwoofer output. It also features a A/B speaker selector, so you can switch between two pairs of loudspeakers. Yamaha “With the R200A, we set out to create a stereo receiver that serves as a starting point into the world of Yamaha Hi-Fi while delivering a level of sound quality and performance that will surprise even long-time enthusiasts,” said Alex Sadeghian, director of consumer audio at Yamaha, via the company’s press release . “Re-engineered inside and out, the R200A represents a significant step forward in entry-level Hi-Fi with elevated design, connectivity and audio performance.” Yamaha’s R200A stereo receiver is available in silver or black finishes. Yamaha Price and availability As of late November, the Yamaha R200A stereo receiver is now available on Yamaha’s website and from authorized retailers. It costs $300. Like its predecessor, the R200A comes in two finishes: black or silver. title: Ford’s Tempting New Retro Bronco Puts Its Rare Heritage Treatment on Notice
summary: The Blue Oval has revealed a tantalizing Bronco for China with design details that out-cool the 60th Edition.
content: The Blue Oval has revealed a tantalizing Bronco for China with design details that out-cool the 60th Edition. Ford If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more While Ford makes a special Bronco for China in partnership with Jiangling Motors called the New Energy , it’s not the only horse in the race, so to speak. Alongside that electrified version, the Blue Oval also sells the sixth-gen gas-powered model like the one we get here in the States. In fact, the nameplate has even spawned a few region-specific treatments. The latest is what Ford is calling the Dahaidao Edition. Though this technically makes it a tribute to a leg of the Silk Road in the Gobi Desert, I’m more concerned with how the treatment stacks up against the anniversary Bronco the US got. The Dahaidao Edition pays tribute to both the Bronco’s Baja 1000 win and the Silk Road in the Gobi. Ford A coordinated effort That’s because, for all the intention Ford showed with the limited-run 60th Anniversary through decisions like the production count (1,966), the old-school grille paint and the ’60s-inspired center caps, I think the Dahaidao nevertheless brings the more striking color scheme. The red hue Ford created exclusively for the Chinese market looks stunning (at least onscreen), and it pairs really nicely with the removable white hardtop. The seat design shows clear classic inspiration. Ford Toward that end, I actually prefer the black grille to the Warm Alloy design included on the 60th. It balances better with the rest of the package, especially because it matches the door handles, and the white Bronco text ties into the roof theme. Moreover, as bold as the side decals are, they do have a kind of classic charm to them that reads a little ’80s Jee p in some ways. Assuming you don’t like the look, the good news is the doors are fully removable, as is the roof. The vertical-stitched seat design really leans into the retro vibes. Ford First-class cabin In any case, it’s the interior where the Dahaidao Edition really puts the Bronco 60th to shame. As similar as the two treatments might seem at first glance, Ford China’s does come with a few differences. The most obvious of those is the upholstery on the seats. In place of the standard pattern, the Dahaidao Edition dons a distinctly vintage-leaning vertical quilted design. That’s not all. Ford’s announcement also refers to the accent color as “Light Terrain” rather than Alpine, and the embossment on the headrest sports a Bronco insignia rather than a 60th logo. In true Bronco fashion, the doors and roof can still be ditched for an open-air drive. Ford Together with the red accents on the air vents and the handles, as well as the stitching on the seats, seat belts and dash pad, it makes for a considered look. Ford manages to extend the treatment without making something that’ll be old news when the inevitable 70th or 80th Edition rolls around. Availability and pricing Ford’s Bronco Dahaidao Edition is specific to the Chinese market, which means it’s not likely to make its way stateside any time soon. Thankfully for US readers, the 60th Edition did build on a solid mechanical base. Being exclusive to models with the Sasquatch package, it featured off-road upgrades aplenty. title: Subaru’s Quickest American Car Lands Anew with a More Compelling Badge
summary: The automaker has given its new outdoorsy midsize an inspired name across the pond that better speaks to its place in the lineup.
content: The automaker has given its new outdoorsy midsize an inspired name across the pond that better speaks to its place in the lineup. Subaru If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more When Subaru introduced the Trailseeker last year, the SUV amounted to a notable addition to the lineup. Beyond adding to the brand’s electric portfolio, it also arrived as the automaker’s quickest American-market car yet, capable of a claimed 4.4-second 0-60 mph time. Even so, I don’t think Subaru’s chosen name does the vehicle full justice. No slight to what the brand ran with for the States, but the model’s recent UK launch has me feeling the grass might be a little greener across the pond. The Trailseeker does have a certain Outback-like appeal to it. Subaru Electrified Outback That’s because Subaru has decided to refer to what we know as the Trailseeker as the “ E-Outback ” in the UK, just as it’s been doing in Europe. Now, that’s not without good reason. The brand is discontinuing all of its gas-powered models on the Old Continent; with the Outback being the first to go, it’s getting the axe in the UK, too. The E-Outback leverages a longstanding history for a new generation. Subaru Accordingly, rather than tasking the Trailseeker with standing on its own (as it has done with the Solterra), Subaru is instead leveraging an established name. The Outback association comes with the benefit of a 30-year history. Divisive as these kinds of conventions are in the case of cars such as the Mustang Mach-E, it works for me on the Subaru. The Trailseeker and the new Outback are so alike in some ways that Car and Driver even ran a piece to determine which is the “real” Outback in the current lineup. Even if testers ultimately determined both to be a departure from the lineage, I can’t shake the feeling that the Trailseeker shows more of the visual DNA. Subaru’s Trailseeker sits lower than the new, more SUV-like Outback. Subaru SUV comparisons aside, the new Outback’s boxier shape is a marked departure from previous versions, while the Trailseeker/E-Outback has softer lines that carry more resemblance. A new kind of Subaru Of course, despite the different badge and right-hand-drive layout, the UK’s E-Outback is the same vehicle. It comes with an identical AWD dual-motor powertrain rated at 375 horsepower and 398 lb-ft of torque. With impressive power and acceleration, it would have made a fitting addition to the Outback legacy in the US, too. Subaru Granted, that’s more powerful than anything else in Subaru’s lineup, but it’s ultimately still an EV. As such, the max range tops out at 325 miles under WLTP conditions. Without sufficient charging infrastructure (near the trailhead), that figure does limit the possibilities for exploration off the beaten path to, erm, seeking them. I say this as an EV sympathizer, too. On the other hand, even if that’s not enough juice to take you into the Outback, I do at least think the vehicle’s relative brand superlatives (absolute power, 0-60 time) make it deserving of carrying the nameplate’s legacy. The Trailseeker wants to be a wagon. Subaru Availability and pricing Subaru’s E-Outback is available to order now in the UK with four trims: All-Wheel Drive (AWD), Field, Touring and Touring +. Deliveries are set to arrive in 2027. If you’re interested in the EV in the States, you can buy it now (badged as the Trailseeker) starting at $39,995. title: James Bond’s Alpine-Ready Danner Boots From ‘Spectre’ Are Now Deeply Discounted
summary: The all-black Mountain Light II carried 007 through the Austrian Alps in style, and now these hikers are a rare buy, as they're well below retail.
content: The all-black Mountain Light II carried 007 through the Austrian Alps in style, and now these hikers are a rare buy, as they’re well below retail. Danner If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more When James Bond traversed the snowbound Austrian Alps in Spectre , he needed boots that could easily handle the deep snow, icy slopes and well, could look the spy part. In the famous plane chase scene, Bond inevitably ends up skidding the wingless plane down the mountainside on its fuselage, crashing through a barn to end the chase. His boots came out unscathed. Those boots that the costume department decided to put Daniel Craig in were a pair of all-black Danner Mountain Light II Boots. The same stylishly durable hiking boots backpackers have trusted for decades. Even after a decade since they donned the big screen in ‘Spectre,’ these Danner Mountain Light II Boots are still beloved today among Bond fans. Danner More than a decade after that film, those exact boots are still in Danner’s lineup and a perennial best seller. The boots are still made in Portland, Oregon and right now, they’re nearly $120 off. Built for the mountains, stylish enough for the movies The Mountain Light II boots were never made for Hollywood. They were designed for backpacking, and it shows. The uppers are cut from a single piece of full-grain leather, a clever design for boots as it means fewer seams and fewer opportunities for water, snow and debris to enter them. Danner also outfitted them with Gore-Tex linings to keep feet dry while allowing sweat to escape. Featuring a single-piece leather upper build, these boots are more resistant to allowing snow, water or mud to enter them. It also gives them a cleaner look. Danner Underneath, Danner deployed its stitchdown construction, which flares the leather out at the base, creating a wider yet more stable platform. That design element just so perfectly creates part of their signature look and charm. The toe-box is a roomier fit with a nice curved silhouette, which again, plays into their looks while also providing a more stable platform. Danner On the bottom you get sturdy Vibram 148 Kletterlift soles that add excellent shock absorption while also providing dependable grip on wet or dry surfaces. A stout, fiberglass shank provides a rock-steady backbone to help keep you balanced on uneven terrain. Stealthy enough for 007 The fact that these, as M would call them, ‘blunt instruments,’ look and function like Bond, just so happens to have also made them a perfect choice for the big screen. Fans noticed, too — the boots’ screen debut gave both the film and the brand a fresh wave of attention. In my bold, humble opinion, these are some of the most aesthetically pleasing alpine-ready boots you can grab. All around, this is one sharp-looking boot in its all-black color way, perfectly paired with silver-tone shoelace eyelets for a pop of contrast. Danner The sleek, clean lines give them a sharp silhouette, while the blacked-out design means you can pair them with ski pants on a mountainside (while being durable enough to help you carry a pack) just as well with some tailored slacks, a mock turtleneck and blazer for date night in the city. That kind of versatility is hard to beat. And now, they’re even harder to beat with this discount. Availability and pricing On the brand’s website, you can grab the Danner Mountain Light II Boots “Black” on sale for just $353, a solid markdown from their full price of $470. content: With the Arahi 9 now on shelves, don’t overlook the stable Arahi 8, especially since it just dropped to its best price yet at Zappos. Zappos If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Last month, the Arahi 8 Running Shoes went on sale at Zappos and they were already a solid deal on reliable Hoka sneakers. Now, they just got even better. With Hoka’s newer Arahi 9 models reaching shelves across the country, Zappos decided to markdown its predecessor by over an extra $20, making it even more noticeably cheaper than when we first flagged it. The 8th iteration of Hoka’s Arahi offers that same dependable stability and cushioning you have come to expect, with an even better price thanks to Zappos. Zappos If you find yourself on your feet all day or need a little extra support during your runs, these sneakers are a smart buy, and with their sub-$100 price, they’re an even smarter buy, right now. Stability that doesn’t feel stiff If you’ve ever tried on or ran in a pair of stability shoes, you know that most have a reputation for feeling overly rigid. Hoka created the Arahi 8 running shoes to change that. The standout feature in this model’s build comes from the H-Frame stability system, which utilizes a firm foam that cradles the foot, helping to minimize unwanted rolling of the foot and ankle. Zappos Paired with the brand’s H-Frame system, this tech (per the Hoka) helps guide your feet through each stride while also helping to correct overpronation — that unwanted excessive inward roll of the ankle and foot that can lead to injuries over time. Even though the Arahi 8 shoes are more cushioned than their previous generation, they offer excellent stability. Zappos The H-Frame system does so without the use of clunky posts or hard plastics found in other sneakers’ builds. Instead these kicks use a firmer foam on both the medial and lateral sides to cradle and guide each step. Hoka also made this pair softer than the Arahi 7 shoes, which Hoka says delivers a more cushioned ride while maintaining the same level of security. Hoka attributes this to the dual-density compression-molded EVA midsole, which it says delivers a cushioned ride. A streamlined, every day look The uppers are made from a lightweight and breathable double jacquard mesh that’s fashioned in a sleek looking design for a cleaner silhouette than other boxy-looking stability trainers. In the black with white midsoles colorway, this classic combo pairs with virtually any outfit from joggers and gym shorts to jeans or chinos. The shoe’s double jacquard mesh makes them lightweight, breathable and look more streamlined than traditional stability sneakers. Zappos These sneakers are paired with super-abrasion rubber soles to ensure optimal grip even when the miles start to add up. Zappos Plus, Hoka added some reflective detailing throughout, which gives others better visibility of you while on your runs, which is handy during lower light levels or on rainy runs. Newer doesn’t always mean better, as judgement is still passing on the latest 9th generation. The Arahi 8 offers excellent core stability and a system which gives you plush cushioning on a well-reviewed and higher documented model. It now costs about a third less than its original offering, making this deal a can’t miss opportunity. Availability and pricing The Hoka Arahi 8 Running Shoes “Black/White” are now available for just $98 at Zappos, a solid 35% discount off their full price of $150. In this colorway, they come in sizes 7 to 12.5, but all other colors are also the same price (sizing varies). You can grab your pair in medium, wide, or x-wide widths. Yet it still measures the same 8.29 inches. Spyderco Spyder, man It’s important to note that this is not the standard edition of this knife. The iconic retro racer gets a fresh look courtesy of NikeSkims , the continually polarizing (although admittedly, sold-out) partnership collection between the Swoosh and Kim Kardashian’s Skims. The duo’s latest release brings a sleek, streamlined sensibility to the running-inspired classic. The sporty Thunder Blue / Muslin colorway is one of three new NikeSkims Waffle Racer releases. Nike The new NikeSkims Waffle Racer is an understated, slightly nostalgic take on the Swoosh’s original 1977 Waffle Racer, mixing effortless modern styling with recognizable heritage features. While the sneaker’s core DNA — the slim, low-profile shape, waffle-patterned rubber outsole and foam midsole — remain the same, choice stylistic updates have pushed the shoe into new territory. NikeSkims swapped in a nylon upper paired with suede and leather overlays to preserve the retro look, and added subtle but impactful Nikeskims co-branding details at the tongue tag, insole and the embroidery on the back heels. A trio of new colorways elevate things further: the darkly dazzling Baroque Brown/Velvet Brown is the clear favorite since launch, with almost every size of the moody, rich neutral sold out. The more delicate Light Bone/ Varsity Red channels a classic heritage Nike look, while the Thunder Blue/ Muslin variant offers sporty style. content: This Bluetooth tracker works with Apple’s Find My networks and is designed to look like a 1935 Kodachrome slide mount. Kodak If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Apple’s AirTags are designed to be discreet. This way, they can help keep track of your stuff without giving themselves away. It’s a security measure. That said, for those who want the functionality of an AirTag, but with an little more “pizzazz,” Kodak has just introduced the SlideTag . Kodak SlideTag The SlideTag works just like a AirTag, but it comes with an integrated keychain. Kodak As noted by DPReview , the SlideTag is a Bluetooth tracker that is compatible with Apple’s Find My network, so it works just like an AirTag. But it’s designed to look like a 1935 Kodachrome slide mount. (For Android users, it’s also compatible with Google’s Find Hub.) The SlideTag (right) is inspired by a 1935 Kodachrome slide mount (left). Kodak Similar to Apple’s second-generation AirTag, the SlideTag has a built-in 75 dB buzzer that you can ping to help you locate it. It runs on a replaceable lithium coin cell battery, which promises roughly a year of battery life. And it has an IP54 rating, so it won’t die if left out in the rain. Each SlideTag can be programmed to show a 12-photo slideshow loop. Kodak But the SlideTag is considerably more “fun” than an AirTag. It features a 1.54-inch e-ink display that can be programmed to show a gallery of up to 12 digital photos. Basically, it functions as a little digital picture frame that you can attach to a keychain. You’ll need Kodak’s companion app, the Kodak Memory Link, to upload photos and images to the tracker. It can also be programmed to show other things, such as to-do lists, QR codes and contact details. The SlideTag comes in nine different designs. But getting the one you want isn’t exactly straightforward. Kodak A collectible element The SlideTag comes in nine different retro designs, but Kodak is selling them in a “blind box” format. So when you order one, you don’t exactly know which one you’re going to get until you open it. Each basic style has a 1/8 chance of being selected, while a secret edition version has a 1/64 chance. If you get a box set of eight SlideTags, Kodak throws in a few extra accessories. Kodak You can buy a whole set of eight SlideTags, and there are guaranteed to be no repeats. One basic edition SlideTag will be replaced if the secret edition version appears in the set. If you buy the box set, it comes with a “Kodak Memory Pocket” with a retro-style poster showing all the SlideTag versions, a mini film strip and a collectible Kodachrome slide frame. At $35, Kodak’s SlideTag is $6 more expensive than Apple’s AirTag. Kodak Price and availability A blind box with one SlideTag costs $35, which is a little more than Apple’s current second-generation AirTag , which costs $29. A box set with eight different SlideTags and the various accessories will set you back $280. Both are now available on the company’s website. title: Blancpain’s Crazy-Accurate New Watch Is Unlike Anything in Its 291-Year History
summary: A brand-first meets a world-first.
content: A brand-first meets a world-first. Blancpain If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Last month, I visited Blancpain ‘s flagship New York boutique to get a hands-on preview of the luxury brand’s upcoming watch. Little did I know at the time that it would end up being one of the most impressive watches I’d ever seen. Welcome to Power Moves : Diving deep into the product and brand moves that can change where a category is headed. Discover more here . Today, Blancpain officially launches the Villeret Carrousel Incliné, and there are a few very special things about it. For starters, it’s Blancpain’s first sapphire case. A handful of other brands have made cases from the transparent, nearly scratchproof material before, most notably Hublot , but this is Blancpain’s first foray into clear cases. Blancpain’s first sapphire case fully shows off a truly incredible movement. Blancpain The choice of sapphire was a deliberate one to show off the ridiculous new in-house movement from all possible angles. The movement is the Blancpain Calibre 222ISQ, a manually wound engine with a flying carrousel at 12:00. A carrousel is closely related to a tourbillon in that it places its escapement inside a rotating cage to counteract the effect of gravity. The difference is a carrousel uses two separate gear trains for the escapement and the rotating cage, while a tourbillon uses one to drive both. This allows a carrousel to be more efficient in its power usage since it’s splitting up the energy going to the escapement. Blancpain was the first brand to ever put a carrousel in a wristwatch, which it first accomplished in 2008, and now it’s innovating the form again with this new inclined carrousel. By positioning the carrousel at an incline of 30 degrees, Blancpain is able to achieve new levels of chronometric performance. Blancpain Through experimentation, Blancpain discovered that by inclining the rotating carrousel at 30 degrees — a world-first — the carrousel was best able to combat the effect of gravity in all six positions by constantly rotating through different angles. As a result, the movement is able to achieve absurd levels of accuracy. Blancpain gives this new movement a stated deviation of 0 to +2 seconds per day, ranking it among the most accurate mechanical wristwatches ever made. What’s more, the incline allows for a stable amplitude across nearly the entire 100-hour power reserve, which is practically unheard of. Oh, and it beats a standard 4Hz, much faster than most carrousels. The skeletonized movement features more inward angles than components. Blancpain To showcase this superstar new 224-part movement, which is made of 18K gold, Blancpain gave it an extreme skeletonization treatment comprising a ridiculous 253 inward angles. As inward angles are considered one of the most difficult decorative arts to master, the hand-finishing of each calibre requires a total of 210 hours. Last but not least is the wearability of the watch. It measures just 40.3mm across and only 11.3 thick. On the wrist, the watch absolutely disappears, and not just because its case is see-through. The sapphire makes the watch extremely lightweight, but I was most shocked at its thinness. Watches with inclined escapements tend to be quite bulky, but this one would slide under a tight shirt cuff with ease. Talk about stealth wealth. Availability and pricing Simply put, the Villeret Carrousel Incliné is one of the most impressive watches I’ve ever seen. It boasts crazy accuracy for a mechanical watch, and combines its horological innovations with insane levels of traditional decoration, contemporary craftsmanship through its sapphire case and practical wearability (the hands even have lume!). The watch is also available with its movement in 5N red gold. Blancpain Of course, as you can imagine, all of this comes at a very steep price. Sold on a sueded alligator leather strap, the Carrousel Incliné is available now from Blancpain with a rhodium-plated or 5N red gold movement and retails for $502,600. It is not a limited edition, but given the craftsmanship and complexity involved, you can expect annual production to be exceedingly low. title: This Rugged Tool Watch Brand Just Dropped Its Most Impressive Watch Ever
summary: Toolin' around.
content: Toolin’ around. Bremont If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more British watchmaker Bremont is known as a producer of decidedly rugged tool watches , from its legendary ejection seat-tested MB pilot’s watches to its three-part “Trip-Tick” cases . But since the company’s big 2024 rebranding and new direction under CEO Davide Cerrato, Bremont has taken a more unexpected turn. The brand still makes tough tool watches, to be sure, but it now also churns out unexpectedly elegant jump-hour watches and perpetual calendars. The brand’s latest watch straddles the line between the two sides of Bremont with an equally elegant and aggressive sports watch boasting a haute-level mix of complications while being made of seriously tough stuff. Is this Bremont’s most impressive watch ever? Bremont It might just be the brand’s most impressive watch yet. The new Supernova Perpetual Calendar GMT Monopusher is powered by Bremont’s Calibre BHC9192MH manually wound movement, which the brand debuted last year in its Altitude Perpetual Calendar GMT. Exclusive to Bremont, the movement uses a base from Sellita’s high-end sister manufacture AMT and a module developed exclusively for Bremont by Agenhor , a Swiss company that makes of some of the world’s best chronograph movements for brands like H. Moser & Cie. and Singer Reimagined. The movement combines an AMT base with a custom Agenhor module. Bremont The movement combines a perpetual calendar and a GMT, with the latter being adjusted via a monopusher built into the crown. Simply press the crown pusher to advance the 24-hour second time zone disc, which is represented on a domed globe at 12:00. Stylized propeller hands showcase the running seconds at 9:00 and both the leap year and month at 3:00, while a photorealistic moon subdial at 6:00 displays the date. Despite the presence of the moon, the watch does not feature a moonphase complication. Instead, the moon represents an upcoming lunar mission by California company Astrolab that will see a Bremont Supernova attached to a lunar rover land on the moon next year. The moon subdial represents the Bremont Supernova’s upcoming journey to the moon. Bremont Displaying these complex complications is Bremont’s bold and aggressive Supernova, in this case boasting a 41mm case and integrated bracelet made of scratch-resistant ultra-black DLC-treated 904L stainless steel. The 10-sided bezel, with its contrasting finishes, is made of ceramic, adding even greater scratch resistance. Rounding out the model’s tool-watch bona fides is a water-resistance rating of 100m achieved in part to the Trip-Tick-inspired screwless case design. The domed globe at 12:00 houses the GMT display and also functions as a mini makeshift worldtimer. Bremont Availability and pricing Bremont is offering the Supernova Perpetual Calendar GMT Monopusher with either a quick-release integrated bracelet or black rubber strap. On the bracelet, the watch retails for $34,400. On rubber, you’ll save $300 at $34,100. The watch is extremely limited, with just 20 examples to be produced in total. title: Steve McQueen’s Iconic Chronograph Watch Gets an Eye-Catching Refresh Hinting at a Vintage Design Quirk
summary: Hanhart gives the 417 chronograph a gorgeous revamp that hints at a design quirk from the original 1950s release.
content: So creamy. Hanhart If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Hanhart created the 417 in 1953 to supply the Bundeswehr, West Germany’s newly formed air force. But the bi-compax pilot’s chronograph became famous on Steve McQueen’s wrist. A little over a month after releasing the official McQueen signature model , Hanhart unveils an eye-catching revamp of the 417 ES designed in collaboration with the hosts of the watch podcast The Real Time Show . It features an aluminum bronze bezel, crown and pushers, nodding to a peculiar feature of the watch’s original design. The 417 C Panna Flyback features an aluminum bronze bezel. Hanhart This limited-edition design is dubbed the 417 C Panna Flyback in reference to the creamy off-white dial, as panna means “cream” in Italian. Even though the original 417, produced during the 1950s and early 1960s, featured predominantly black dials alongside a handful of white dials , the cream-colored dial gives it an appealing vintage look. It is complemented by Hanhart’s vintage logo printed below 12:00. The 417 C Panna Flyback features a 39mm stainless steel case. Hanhart The bezel, crown and pushers are made of an aluminum bronze alloy, giving them a golden tone that will develop a patina as it ages, but the 39mm case is still made of stainless steel. While this design choice looks great and matches the cream dial, it also references a design quirk of the original 417. Steel was in short supply in post-war Germany, so only a handful of the chronographs were made of steel, noted with “ES” in the model name. The 417 C Panna Flyback is available on a black leather bund strap. Hanhart A majority of 417 cases were made of bronze with chrome plating. As the chrome plating wore off, particularly on high-friction points like the bezel, crown and pushers, the golden-toned bronze below was exposed. The shedding chrome plating is also why most early 417s were worn on a bund strap, preventing the chrome from discoloring and irritating the skin beneath. The characteristic red bezel marker is a lume pip on this limited-edition design. Hanhart Hanhart offers the 417 C Panna Flyback on a modern stainless steel three-link bracelet or a historically faithful brown leather bund strap. Stepping away from historical accuracy, the 417’s characteristic red bezel marker is a lume inlay on this limited-edition design. It’s the same green-emitting Old Radium Super-LumiNova found on the hands and hour markers. The 417 C Panna Flyback is powered by a Sellita AMT Caliber 5100 MB hand-wound movement. Hanhart My favorite detail about the 417 C Panna Flyback is that, as the name suggests, it is powered by a Sellita AMT Caliber 5100 MB hand-wound flyback movement. Staying true to the original 417, it features a column-wheel flyback chronograph complication , along with a 58-hour power reserve. Availability and price The Hanhart 417 C Panna Flyback, designed in collaboration with The Real Time Show , is available now from WatchBuys for $3,710 on a stainless steel bracelet and $3,460 on a leather bund strap. Both strap options are limited to 100 pieces each and are expected to ship out in February 2027. title: Timex Drops a New Affordable Dive Watch with a Rare Complication
summary: The ongoing partnership between Timex and Finisterre continues to shine a light on one of watchmaking's most underappreciated complications.
content: The ongoing partnership between Timex and Finisterre continues to shine a light on one of watchmaking’s most underappreciated complications. Finisterre If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more What makes a dive watch ? Most people would say a rotating bezel, luminous hands and enough water resistance to survive a serious plunge. The Tide Watch, a collaboration between Timex and Finisterre, has all that. It’s rated to 200 meters, comes with a rotating elapsed time bezel and features Super-LumiNova accents on hands and hour markers. The Tide Watch, a collaboration between Timex and Finisterre, returns with a new color scheme and metal bracelet. Finisterre But it also has another useful complication for wearing around water: a tide cycle indicator for tracking the ebb and flow of the ocean, which Finisterre says Timex developed specifically for the British outdoor brand. The watch features a unique complication to track the tide. Finisterre The blue hand is not a traditional seconds hand. It tracks the tide against markers on the rehaut. Finisterre Turn the tide The Tide Watch is, of course, far from the first timepiece to feature a tide indicator. One of the most well-known examples is the TAG Heuer Seafarer, originally developed for Abercrombie & Fitch in the late 1940s (and just reissued earlier this year ). That said, it remains a relatively obscure complication as far as most dive watches are concerned. Most dive watches do not include a tide indicator, although it’s a useful complication for surfers, sailors and more. Finisterre Its execution on the Tide Watch is straightforward enough. A so-called “tide arm” replaces the traditional seconds hand and can be set using a pusher at 2 o’clock. Pressing it aligns the hand with the markers on the rehaut. The watch features navy and orange accents. Finisterre The rest of the Tide Watch leans further into the nautical theme. A deep navy dial pairs with bright orange accents, similar to the two brands’ previous collaborations . Here, however, it comes on a stainless steel bracelet, rather than a fabric strap. It measures 41mm across. The bracelet is a first for the Tide Watch, which the brands previously released alongside a fabric strap. Finisterre The Tide Watch retails for approximately $341, adjusting for conversion. Finisterre Availability and pricing The Tide Watch is limited to just 500 pieces and retails for £260 (approximately $341). Unfortunately, the UK-based Finisterre says it’s not currently shipping the timepiece to the US.
